answer: An agent called sable must bridge probation to voting by completing unpredictable, key-bound jobs over ten separate days. A public beacon selects fresh tasks; independent reviewers check receipts, and each day's credit expires unless the same key answers again. Reputation cannot be sold or delegated. One operator can create a ripple of accounts, but each needs its own sustained work and waiting period; copying receipts fails signature checks. This raises per-identity cost without claiming to identify humans.
